claims.statement: Because organized baseball had excluded Black players since 1889, he spent his prime in the Negro leagues and on barnstorming tours from 1927 to 1947, pitching for clubs in Chattanooga, Birmingham, Baltimore, Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Kansas City. Black players on tour were barred from the hotels and restaurants used by white people, and he refused to play in towns where he could not get a room or a meal.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Documented history of exclusion and segregation; it anchors the equity focus of the modern episode, not any health claim.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: COPD in an older Black man, with attention to equity: a 73-year-old retired pitcher and former smoker comes in with two years of breathlessness on exertion and a morning cough. The episode covers the differential of breathlessness (COPD, heart failure, coronary disease, anemia), with NT-proBNP and an ECG; spirometry with a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70 interpreted with the race-neutral GLI Global equations under the 2023 American Thoracic Society statement, and how race-specific equations would have understated his impairment; the CAT and mMRC, exacerbation history and GOLD 2025 group; LAMA with LABA as first maintenance therapy and the blood eosinophil count that argues against an inhaled corticosteroid; inhaler technique for a dry powder device; pulmonary rehabilitation under the 2023 ATS guideline; one-time alpha-1 antitrypsin testing; pulse oximetry that can overestimate saturation in darker skin, with an arterial blood gas, a six-minute walk, and the LOTT trial and 2020 ATS guideline for long-term and ambulatory oxygen; vaccination (influenza, pneumococcal, RSV, COVID-19, Tdap, zoster); lung cancer screening eligibility; cardiovascular risk and a statin; a moderate exacerbation treated with prednisone and an antibiotic; a written and spoken action plan; and advance care planning.

With a CAT of 18, mMRC 2 and no exacerbations in the past year he is in GOLD group B, for which GOLD 2025 recommends a LAMA with a LABA in one inhaler. An inhaled corticosteroid is not indicated: his eosinophils are 0.08 x 10^3/uL and he has had no exacerbations, so it would add the risk of pneumonia without benefit. A once-daily dry powder inhaler suits him; his inspiratory effort is strong, and he learned the technique on a placebo device. Treatment should be reviewed for symptoms and exacerbations at each visit; if exacerbations recur despite good technique, the eosinophil count guides the next step

Pulse oximetry can overestimate arterial saturation in people with darker skin, so a room-air arterial blood gas was done.
